'''Marcel Grossmann''' ({{langx|hu|Grossmann Marcell}}; April 9, 1878 – September 7, 1936)<ref>{{Citation|author-first=Louis|author-last=Kollros|author-link =Louis Kollros|title =Prof. Dr. Marcel Grossmann 1878–1936|journal =SchweizerischeNaturforschende Gesellschaft. Verhandlungen|volume =118|pages =325–329|year =1937}}</ref> was a [[Swiss people|Swiss]] [[mathematician]] who was a friend and classmate of [[Albert Einstein]]. Grossmann came from an old Swiss family in [[Zürich]]. His father managed a textile factory. He became a [[Professor]] of Mathematics at the Federal Polytechnic School in Zürich, today the [[ETH Zurich]], specializing in [[descriptive geometry]].

Grossmann was born to a Jewish family in Budapest.
==Career==
In 1900 Grossmann graduated from the [[Federal Polytechnic School]] (ETH) and became an assistant to the geometer [[Wilhelm Fiedler]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Cowen |first=Ron |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vjiPDwAAQBAJ&dq=Marcel+Grossmann+1900+Federal+Polytechnic+School&pg=PA1900 |title=Gravity's Century: From Einstein's Eclipse to Images of Black Holes |date=2019-05-06 |publisher=Harvard University Press |isbn=978-0-674-23928-9}}</ref> He continued to do research on [[non-Euclidean geometry]] and taught in high schools for the next seven years. In 1902, he earned his doctorate from the [[University of Zurich]] with the thesis ''Ueber die metrischen Eigenschaften kollinearer Gebilde'' (translated ''On the Metrical Properties of Collinear Structures'') with Fiedler as advisor. In 1907, he was appointed full professor of descriptive geometry at the Federal Polytechnic School.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Graf-Grossmann |first=Claudia |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RjlfDwAAQBAJ&dq=Marcel+Grossmann+1907&pg=PA96 |title=Marcel Grossmann: For the Love of Mathematics |date=2018-06-08 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-90077-3 |page=96}}</ref>

As a professor of geometry, Grossmann organized summer courses for high school teachers. In 1910, he became one of the founders of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]]. He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1912 at [[Cambridge]]<ref>{{cite book|author=Grossmann, Marcel|chapter=Die Zentralprojektion in der absoluten Geometrie|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the Fifth International Congress of Mathematicians (Cambridge, 22–28 August 1912)|pages=66–69|volume=2|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1912.2/Main/icm1912.2.0066.0069.ocr.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171203153805/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1912.2/Main/icm1912.2.0066.0069.ocr.pdf|archive-date=3 December 2017}}</ref> and in 1920 at [[Strasbourg]].

===Collaborations with Albert Einstein===
[[Albert Einstein]]'s friendship with Grossmann began with their school days in Zürich. Grossmann's careful and complete lecture notes at the Federal Polytechnic School proved to be a salvation for Einstein, who missed many lectures.<ref>Alice Calaprice, Daniel Kennefick, Robert Schulmann, ''An Einstein Encyclopedia'', Princeton University Press, 2015, p. 70.</ref> Grossmann's father helped Einstein get his job at the Swiss Patent Office in [[Bern]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Janssen|first1=Michel|last2=Renn|first2=Jürgen|date=2015-11-19|title=History: Einstein was no lone genius|journal=Nature|volume=527|issue=7578|pages=298–300|doi=10.1038/527298a|pmid=26581276|bibcode=2015Natur.527..298J|doi-access=free}}</ref> and it was Grossmann who helped to conduct the negotiations to bring Einstein back from Prague as a professor of physics at the Zurich Polytechnic. Grossmann was an expert in [[differential geometry]] and [[tensor calculus]], the mathematical tools which would provide a proper mathematical framework for Einstein's work on gravity. Thus, it was natural that Einstein would enter into a scientific collaboration with Grossmann.<ref>J. Earman and C. Glymour, [http://repository.cmu.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1338&context=philosophy  Lost in the Tensors: Einstein's Struggles with Covariance Principles, 1912-1916], footnote page 255; Carnegie Mellon University Research Showcase (accessed February 12, 2016)</ref>

It was Grossmann who emphasized the importance of a non-Euclidean geometry called [[Riemannian geometry]] (also [[elliptic geometry]]) to Einstein, which was a necessary step in the development of Einstein's [[general theory of relativity]]. [[Abraham Pais]]'s book<ref>{{cite book | author=Pais, Abraham |title= [[Subtle is the lord: the science and life of Albert Einstein]] | year=1982}}</ref> on Einstein suggests that Grossmann mentored Einstein in [[tensor]] theory as well. Grossmann introduced Einstein to the [[Ricci_calculus | absolute differential calculus]], started by [[Elwin Bruno Christoffel]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Christoffel |first=E.B. |date=1869 |title=Ueber die Transformation der homogenen Differentialausdrücke zweiten Grades |trans-title=On the transformation of homogeneous differential expressions of the second degree |url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=GDZPPN002153882&IDDOC=266356 |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik |language=German |volume=70 |pages=46–70}}</ref> and fully developed by [[Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro]] and [[Tullio Levi-Civita]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ricci |first1=Gregorio |last2=Levi-Citiva |first2=Tullio |date=March 1900 |title=Méthodes de calcul différentiel absolu et leurs applications |trans-title=Methods of absolute differential calculus and their applications |url=https://zenodo.org/record/1428270 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=French |publisher=Springer |volume=54 |issue=1–2 |pages=125–201 |doi=10.1007/BF01454201 |s2cid=120009332}}</ref> Grossmann facilitated Einstein's unique synthesis of mathematical and theoretical physics in what is still today considered the most elegant and powerful theory of gravity: the general theory of relativity. The collaboration of Einstein and Grossmann led to a ground-breaking paper, "Outline of a Generalized Theory of Relativity and of a Theory of Gravitation", which was published in 1913 and was one of the two fundamental papers which established Einstein's theory of gravity.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Einstein |first1=A. |last2=Grossmann |first2=M. |author-link2=Marcel Grossmann |year=1913 |title=Entwurf einer verallgemeinerten Relativitätstheorie und einer Theorie der Gravitation |trans-title=Outline of a Generalized Theory of Relativity and a Theory of Gravitation |journal=Zeitschrift für Mathematik und Physik |language=German |volume=62 |pages=225–261, 245–261}}</ref>

==Death==
Grossmann died of [[multiple sclerosis]] in 1936.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Goldsmith |first1=Donald |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zGzcV40b3IkC&dq=Marcel+Grossmann+multiple+sclerosis&pg=PA34 |title=E = Einstein: His Life, His Thought, and His Influence on Our Culture |last2=Bartusiak |first2=Marcia |date=August 2008 |publisher=Sterling Publishing Company, Inc. |isbn=978-1-4027-6319-9 |page=34}}</ref> The community of relativists celebrates Grossmann's contributions to physics by organizing [[ICRANet#Marcel Grossmann meetings|Marcel Grossmann meetings]] every three years.

== Legacy ==
The [[International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics]] presents the [[International Center for Relativistic Astrophysics|Marcel Grossmann Awards]]. Each recipient receives a silver casting of the T. E. S. T. sculpture <ref>{{Cite web|title=I.C.R.A. Network - Marcel Grossmann Awards|url=https://www.icranet.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=215&Itemid=332|access-date=2020-09-01|website=www.icranet.org}}</ref> by the artist A. Pierelli. Each year, an institution is selected and between two and six individual scientists are selected. Past institutional winners include the [[Planck (spacecraft)|Planck]] Scientific Collaboration ([[European Space Agency|ESA]]), AlbaNova University Center, [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|Institut des Hautes Etudes Scientifique]] ([[IHES]]) and others. Past individual winners include [[Shing-Tung Yau]], [[Tsung-Dao Lee]], [[Christine Jones Forman]] and [[Stephen Hawking]].
